attestations.reason: the pinned key is the one whose SHA-256 fingerprint equals the carried key's, both fingerprints taken over the key re-encoded after parsing, and every state Verify reads is in that encoding; so wherever the lookup succeeds the two are the same key and verifying with either is the same computation — the pinned key is named in the code to keep the trust flow explicit, and no input short of a SHA-256 collision distinguishes the mutant
